title: Amazon Prime now does something Netflix can’t: Members can watch movies offline
summary: Amazon Prime now allows members to download movies and TV shows for offline viewing on mobile devices, a feature not offered by Netflix. This new perk adds to Prime's existing benefits like free two-day shipping and unlimited streaming, making entertainment accessible without an internet connection for trips or other situations. Users can download content in various quality settings, though offline viewing has a 72-hour window that resets upon reconnecting to the internet.

title: Netflix Stock Clawed by Bears: Are Apple, Hulu, Amazon Threats to Blame?
summary: Netflix stock experienced a significant decline, losing 14% since August 27th, amidst growing fears of increased competition from Apple, Hulu, and Amazon. Investors were spooked by Apple's potential entry into original programming, Hulu's new ad-free tier and a deal to acquire Epix content previously held by Netflix, and Amazon's introduction of offline viewing and expansion into Japan. Despite the sell-off, some analysts remain bullish on Netflix, viewing the competition as beneficial for the streaming market overall.

title: Amazon Is Killing Off the Fire Phone
summary: Amazon has discontinued its Fire Phone, with both 32GB and 64GB models now out of stock and no plans for replenishment. The smartphone, launched last year, failed to gain traction despite Amazon's hopes for the smartphone market. Amazon had previously taken a $170 million charge related to the Fire Phone's poor performance and excessive inventory.

title: Amazon Stops Selling Fire Phone After Struggling to Boost Sales
summary: Amazon has ceased selling its Fire phone after struggling to boost sales since its launch in July 2014. The company had previously written off $170 million in product inventory related to the device. Inventory for the Fire phone is no longer available on Amazon's website or AT&T's online store, coinciding with the introduction of new iPhone models.

title: HP Enterprise: Can it overcome layoffs, split growing pains, and FUD?
summary: HP Enterprise is undergoing a major transformation, splitting from Hewlett-Packard, cutting 25,000 to 30,000 jobs, and focusing on private and hybrid cloud with a goal of $3 billion in annual cloud revenue in 2015. The company faces the challenge of convincing enterprise buyers amidst potential "fear, uncertainty, and doubt" (FUD) from rivals, despite Meg Whitman's plan for a more focused and profitable entity. The main questions revolve around its ability to innovate and provide stability during this significant restructure.

title: The real reason for HP’s woes (and no, it’s not Autonomy)
summary: This article argues that HP's 2008 acquisition of Electronic Data Systems (EDS) for $13.9 billion was a more significant contributor to the company's long-term struggles than the widely criticized 2011 Autonomy purchase. The EDS deal led to an $8 billion write-down and the current challenges faced by HP Enterprise Services, necessitating layoffs and offshoring. While CEO Meg Whitman highlights hybrid cloud growth, HP has fallen out of the public cloud leadership, indicating continued difficulties in the evolving IT landscape.

title: More Details on the XcodeGhost Malware and Affected iOS Apps
summary: This article provides further details on the XcodeGhost malware, which modifies Xcode to infect iOS apps. It discusses the actions taken by Apple, Amazon, and Baidu to mitigate the threat, the discovery of more infected apps, and a deeper technical analysis of how XcodeGhost modifies Xcode and its potential vulnerabilities. The post also offers security suggestions for both iOS users and developers to protect against similar future attacks.

title: Microsoft announces three new console bundles to celebrates first anniversary of Xbox One
summary: Microsoft is celebrating the first anniversary of the Xbox One by introducing three new console bundles. These bundles include a Forza Motorsport 6 Limited Edition console, a 1TB EA Sports FIFA 16 bundle, and an Xbox One Gears of War: Ultimate Edition bundle, offering different games and storage options to cater to various gamers. The bundles are launching on October 2nd, with pre-orders available on Amazon.in.

title: Rackspace Teams Up With Amazon
summary: Rackspace Hosting Inc. is partnering with Amazon.com Inc. to simplify the migration of corporate computing operations to Amazon Web Services (AWS). This collaboration aims to assist corporate customers in moving their data and systems from on-premise facilities to Amazon's cloud platform. The partnership is expected to be officially announced at an upcoming AWS users conference.
